Theorem 1. Let n ≥ 5. If D∗ is a regular n-gon, then every convex n-gon D with
|D| = |D∗ | and vertices sufficiently close to those of D∗ satisfies
                                      τ (D) ≤ τ (D∗ ),
with strict inequality unless D is congruent to D∗ .
Our proof starts from the triangular method introduced by Solynin and Zalgaller in [18]
and recently revisited in [12]. Roughly speaking, the underlying idea is the following.
Assume that a polygon can be partitioned into a family of triangles, each having one side
of the polygon as its base and area proportional to the interior angle opposite to that
base. The torsional rigidity of the polygon can then be bounded from above by the sum
of the mixed torsional rigidities of these triangles, where mixed means that homogeneous
Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed only on the base, while homogeneous Neu-
mann boundary conditions are prescribed on the remaining part of the boundary. The
problem is thus reduced to optimizing the collective behaviour of the mixed torsional
rigidities of these triangles, under a constraint on the sum of their apex angles.
